facts.text: I used Python with pandas, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, and statsmodels to analyze a retweet dataset.
I loaded a CSV file named retweets_congress_115th.csv.gz using pandas.read_csv.
I excluded the full_text column when loading the dataset for speed.
I set dtype for tweet_id_str to str when reading the CSV.
I used index_col='tweet_id_str' when loading the dataset.

The dataset columns included user_id_str, user_screen_name, user_followers_count, created_at, retweet_count, retweeted_status, year, bioguide, birthday, gender, name, state, chamber, party, region, rt_user_id, rt_screen_name, rt_followers_count, rt_bio, age, and age_bucket.
I planned to compute the marginal probability of the party of the tweet and save it to party_marg.
I planned to create a new boolean column is_congress_retweet indicating whether the retweet is coming from a member of Congress.
I planned to get the set of unique user_id_str values using the .unique() method.
I planned to use the .isin(values) method on the rt_user_id column to create is_congress_retweet.
I planned to compute the marginal probability of retweeting a member of Congress and save it to congress_retweet_marg.
I planned to compute counts of retweets by each party and save them to party_cong_retweet_counts.
I planned to calculate and display the joint probability of party and whether the retweet comes from a member of Congress, saving it as party_cong_retweet_joint.
I planned to calculate the conditional probability of retweeting a member of Congress conditioning on the party.
I planned to compute expected joint probabilities under independence using np.outer and save them as party_cong_retweet_indep.

events.text: Loaded and inspected the retweets_congress_115th.csv.gz dataset (shape 209856 by 21) and listed its columns.
Planned Part (a) computation of marginal party probability saved to party_marg.
Planned Part (b) creation of is_congress_retweet and computation of congress_retweet_marg.
Planned Part (c) computation of party_cong_retweet_counts, party_cong_retweet_joint, and conditional probabilities.
Planned Part (d) computation of independence-expected probabilities party_cong_retweet_indep using np.outer.
